content.text: Here's everything you need to know to tune in to Arkansas' Sweet 16 matchup vs. Arizona in the SAP Center.The No. 4-seeded Arkansas Razorbacks (28-8, 13-5, SEC) look to advance to the Elite Eight against the No. 1-seeded Arizona Wildcats (34-2, 16-2, Big 12) on Thursday night. Tip-off from the SAP Center in San Jose (Calif.) is at 8:45 p.m. (CDT), and the game will be televised by CBS.Thursday's matchup will be the ninth between the two programs, with Arkansas leading the all-time series 6-2, including a 3-1 record in neutral-site games. This will be the second time the two teams have faced off in the NCAA Tournament. When they faced off in the 1994 Final Four, the Hogs defeated the Wildcats 91-82. They then advanced to the championship game and defeated Duke to claim their first National Championship.Tip-off between the Hogs and Wildcats is set for 8:45 p.m. (CDT), and the game will be televised by CBS.WHO: No. 4-seeded Arkansas Razorbacks (28-8, 13-5, SEC) vs. No. 1-seeded Arizona Wildcats (34-2, 16-2, Big 12)WHEN: Thursday, Mar. 26, at 8:45 p.m. (CDT)WHERE: SAP Center (17,562) | San Jose, Calif.TV/STREAM: CBSBET SARACEN ODDS: Arkansas +7.5 | Over/Under: 166RADIO STATIONS: Sirius Ch. 99, XM Ch. 190 | Batesville KWOZ-FM 103.3 | Batesville KBTA-AM 1340 | Camden KCXY-FM 95.3 | Camden KAMD-FM 97.1 | Crossett KAGH-AM 800 | Crossett KAGH-FM 104.9 | De Queen KDQN-FM 92.1 | DeWitt KDEW-FM 97.3 | El Dorado KMRX-FM 96.1 | Fayetteville KAKS-FM 99.5 | Fayetteville KUOA-AM 1290 | Fayetteville KQSM-FM 92.1 | Fayetteville KUOA-FM 95.3 | Fayetteville KBVA-FM HD3 106.5 | Forrest City KBFC-FM 93.5 | Fort Smith KERX-FM 95.3 | Glenwood KHGZ-AM 670 | Glenwood KHGZ-FM 98.9 | Hot Springs/Mena KTTG-FM 96.3 | Jonesboro KEGI-FM 100.5 | Little Rock KABZ-FM 103.7 | Magnolia KZHE-FM 100.5 | Marshall KBCN-FM 104.3 | 96.3 Monett (Mo.) Thanks for listening!Sweet 16 Tale of the Tape: Arkansas vs. ArizonaHere's a tale of the tape breakdown of Arkansas basketball's Sweet 16 matchup with No. 1 seed Arizona on Thursday. SAN JOSE — No. 4 seed Arkansas basketball will look to earn a third Elite Eight appearance in the last six years on Thursday night when the Razorbacks face No. 1 seed Arizona in San Jose. Tip-off is set for 8:45 p.m. (CDT), and CBS will have television coverage of the game.The Wildcats are looking to advance past the Sweet 16 round for the first time under head coach Tommy Lloyd. Arizona owns a 34-2 record, the No. 1 overall seed in the West Regional and were cruising in Sunday night's second round game before Utah State went on a 21-7 run from the 14:43 mark to the 6:34 mark of the second half. The Aggies trailed by just four points, 58-54, and wouldn't go away.It wouldn't be enough, though, as Big 12 Player of the Year Jaden Bradley came alive, freshman Brayden Burries provided a dagger three and it was all set up thanks in large to a slew of offensive rebounds from center Motiejus Krivas. In its first round matchup against LIU, Arizona faced little resistance in a 92-58 victory.Thursday's matchup between the Hogs and Cats will be the ninth meeting all-time between the two programs, but it's the first since the 1995-96 season. The Hogs own a 6-2 lead the all-time series over the Wildcats. That last meeting in the 1995-96 season came as part of the Preseason NIT that year, with Arizona beating Arkansas 83-73 in Bud Walton Arena.Most notably, the two teams met in the 1994 Final Four in Charlotte. The Razorbacks got by Arizona 91-82 in the national semifinal game, earning the right to play Duke in the championship game. Arkansas would ultimately go on to beat Duke, 76-72, to win the programs first and only national championship.Ahead of tonight's Sweet NCAA Tournament matchup between fourth seed Arkansas and top seed Arizona here's a 'Tale of the Tape' breakdown of how the two teams stack up, lineup projections, a closer look at the Wildcats and more.To read this full article and more, subscribe now —SALE:50% off first yearGet access to this article and all of the in-depth coverage from the 247Sports Network with this special offer.Join TodayAlready a subscriber? LoginArkansas QBs 'building calluses' with mentality and process in springAs the Arkansas quarterback battle progresses, the focus is on 'building calluses' with the mentality and process through the next stage of spring practices. Arkansas football has been through four spring practices and the quarterback battle remains the big talking point and question mark around Ryan Silverfield's first Razorbacks squad. It's too early to declare a favorite or clubhouse leader, and instead the staff is just focused on making sure each player builds "calluses" with their mentality, approach, decision-making and more through this next stage of spring drills.Silverfield admitted this quarterback competition will take some time to sort out, saying there's a chance it goes through the end of fall camp and up to the first week of the season. With such a long runway in the competition, it's obviously important to stress patience with the development process for each candidate.On Wednesday, quarterbacks coach Mitch Stewart gave insight into the staff's current process with the quarterback room, including the importance of gaining valuable experience through the early stages spring practices."We're in a situation where I think the first three days before spring break is more about just teaching everybody," Stewart said. "Like, this is how we move around practice. This is how we do these drills. This is the verbiage we use, the cadence ... Then, I think now, once we get on the backside of spring break, now it's about building those calluses, right?"For quarterback, obviously, a lot of that has to do with their mentality, building the calluses of their minds, and how they operate and the decisions they make, and putting them in those situations. Coach [Tim Cramsey], I'm gonna tell you, he's one of the best I've ever been around at throwing those guys in situations and seeing how they respond and giving them a chance to build those calluses. And they've responded well to that. It's a cerebral group."Returning redshirt sophomore KJ Jackson and redshirt sophomore Memphis transfer AJ Hill have been the only two to take snaps with the projected starting offense so far this spring, which was expected entering practices. Redshirt senior and Division II transfer Braeden Fuller is still considered a potential darkhorse to win the job after four seasons at Angelo State. The other quarterback in the room is walk-on redshirt freshman Cade Trotter, who transferred to Arkansas after serving as a scout-team quarterback at Clemson last year.Despite the competition in the room and diversity in backgrounds, all four players are rooting for each other to succeed. On top of that, they each have the desire to get better on a daily basis. Stewart shared a couple of examples, including one involving VR goggles over spring break."They're like each other's biggest fans out there on the field," Stewart said. "They have a great sense of urgency to improve. Over the break, they all took VR goggles home with them so that they could watch the first three installs while they were over break. We were joking because one of them said, 'I was running a QB draw and almost ran into the wall. I forgot that I wasn't on the field and all of that, my mom's like hey stop'. But those are the type of kids that they are. They're constantly sending you texts wanting to know, 'Hey, what does this play look like? Is this right?' Those types of things."All four quarterbacks each bring a unique skillset to the position and provide something different than the rest of the room, according to Stewart."Obviously KJ has a unique skill set," Stewart said. "Dude's very athletic, but he's very cerebral too. He's just a kind of a savvy ball player. You can tell he's been around a lot of ball, kind of comes natural to him. ... Then AJ, obviously I've got a lot of experience with him being around him. Another very, very high cerebral kid, very smart football player. He's one of those that has that unique skill set of taking what you see on film, and he can do that out on the grass. He can see that blitz coming and a lot of people can't do that. It's one thing to see it on a big projector. It's another thing to see it coming when you're there. "Then you got Braeden, who's played a lot of ball. Braden Fuller, who's a D2 guy, which I'm a former bus leaguer, so me and him have a little kinship there. But he's played a lot of ball, super productive. Then Cade Trotter. There's the fourth dude who's just ultra passionate. That dude, he gets the crowd going, he's a lot of fun. You watch him play ball, that dude is having the time of his life playing football, and it's contagious."Arkansas will be back out on the spring practice field for Day 5 on Thursday afternoon. The Razorbacks have 12 practice sessions left this spring, culminating with the annual Spring Game on Saturday April 25 at 2 p.m. (CDT) in Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium.
